feature_request: The CRM should alert us when our relationship with a country goes cold.

proposed_scope_in: Derive 'last meaningful engagement date' per Country from existing Engagement records (no new data entry); an Engagement counts as meaningful if it is linked to the Country, and has type in a fixed list (meeting, call, mission visit, email logged by staff).
Fixed, system-wide 'cold' rule in v1: no meaningful engagement with a Country in the last 90 days (single constant in config, not a UI screen).
Nightly batch job computing cold/not-cold status per Country, writing status and 'days since last engagement' as derived fields on the Country record.
In-app 'Cold Countries' list view (filter on derived status), sortable by days since last engagement, showing Country, last engagement date, and last contact/owner.
One weekly digest email to each Regional Coordinator listing newly cold countries in their existing region assignment, using the existing Country-to-Coordinator relationship.
Suppression of alerts for Countries with an active Mission or an Engagement scheduled in the future (read from existing Mission/Engagement data) to avoid false alarms.
Alert recipients and visibility inherit the existing Country access model; no new permissions.
proposed_scope_out: Per-country or per-user configurable thresholds and a settings UI (v1 uses one constant; tuning comes after real data).
ML or weighted 'relationship health' scoring, sentiment analysis, or predicted churn.
Reading email/calendar/phone systems for automatic engagement capture (relies only on engagements already logged).
Manual 'snooze', 'acknowledge', or 'mark as intentionally dormant' workflows requiring coordinator input.
Escalation chains, approval workflows, or task assignment from alerts.
Role-level analysis such as tracking whether the specific ministry contact or project lead changed.
Real-time or push/SMS/chat notifications; only in-app list plus weekly email.
New tables for relationship history, alert state, or historical role graphs.
Judging diplomatic sensitivity of why a relationship is quiet (policy for humans, not the product).

assumptions.statement: 'Cold' means a lack of recent logged engagement, not a qualitative judgment of relationship quality.
assumptions.rationale: Engagement history already exists in the CRM, so a time-since-last-engagement rule is deterministic, explainable, and needs no new data entry or models.

assumptions.statement: A single global threshold (90 days) is acceptable for v1 across ~100 countries.
assumptions.rationale: Avoids a configuration UI and per-country tuning tables; one constant can be changed by engineering after the first release based on observed alert volume.

assumptions.statement: The audience is Operations and Regional Coordinators, who need a prioritized list and a weekly digest rather than real-time alerts.
assumptions.rationale: A weekly digest plus list view fits the pace of relationship decay, minimizes notification fatigue, and needs only a simple scheduled job.

assumptions.statement: Existing Engagement records are logged reasonably consistently, and the Country-to-Coordinator assignment and Country/Mission access model already exist and can be reused.
assumptions.rationale: Reusing existing entities means no new schema, no extra coordinator data entry, and no custom RBAC.

assumptions.statement: Some countries are legitimately quiet (e.g., no active projects), and an occasional false positive is tolerable in v1 if the alert is informational and does not trigger any action.
assumptions.rationale: Accepting imperfect precision lets us ship without manual dormant flags; the active-mission and scheduled-engagement suppression catches the most obvious cases cheaply.

success_criteria: Nightly job completes for all ~100 Countries in under 10 minutes and the Cold Countries list matches an independent SQL check of the 90-day rule for 100% of a sampled 20 countries in UAT.
Zero new required fields for Regional Coordinators: no new mandatory data entry in any existing form.

Weekly digest is delivered to 100% of Regional Coordinators who have at least one newly cold country, with no more than 15 countries listed per coordinator on average in the first 4 weeks (a signal the threshold is not too noisy).
In a 4-week pilot, at least 50% of countries flagged cold receive a new logged Engagement within 30 days of first alert, as an observable indicator that alerts prompt action.
Feature ships as derived fields plus one list view plus one email job, with no new tables.

challenges.challenge_text: The weekly digest and 'Cold Countries' list inherit the 'existing Country access model', but the list shows 'last contact/owner' and the digest is sent by email. A Regional Coordinator for Region X, or a staff member scoped to only a few countries, could see contact names for countries outside their assignment if the list view or batch-written derived fields on Country bypass per-record permission checks. The digest also puts country names and contact identities into email, which leaves the CRM's access controls and may be forwarded or retained in personal mailboxes. If a coordinator's access is revoked after reassignment, the digest could still arrive. Needs explicit enforcement: list query filtered by the viewer's country scope, digest content minimal (country name and days only, no contact names), and recipients re-evaluated at send time.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: Proposer asserts 'no new permissions' but has not shown that the nightly job's derived fields, list view, and email path each apply the existing scope check. The email channel is not covered by the existing access model at all.

challenges.challenge_text: Alert fatigue: 'occasional false positive is tolerable' is unsupported, and there is no snooze or dormant flag. Many of ~100 countries are legitimately low-touch (no active projects, small partners), so the same countries will reappear on the list every week and coordinators will learn to ignore the digest. The 'newly cold' wording is also ambiguous, since without alert state (no new tables) the job cannot reliably tell newly cold from still cold, so it will either re-list the same countries weekly or miss re-crossings. Suppression covers only active missions or future engagements. The success criterion of up to 15 countries per coordinator on average is itself a noisy digest. Need a bounded way to identify 'newly cold' (for example a derived field on Country holding the date it first went cold) and a cheap way to exclude known low-touch countries (for example a single boolean on Country set by an admin).
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: Proposer treats false positives as acceptable and excludes any dormant mechanism, but gives no mechanism for newly-cold detection and the stated 15 per coordinator tolerance already implies a noisy digest.

challenges.challenge_text: Equating 'cold' with no logged engagement conflates the relationship with the logging habits of staff. Countries whose engagements are held by a coordinator who left, or handled by a delegate who never logs calls, will show cold when the relationship is warm, and a warm-looking country will appear healthy because of one trivial staff-logged email. Also, 'email logged by staff' and any engagement type counting as meaningful lets a bulk or automated mass mailing to 100 countries reset the clock for everyone, hiding genuinely cold countries. Also, engagement records with a null or future date, or merged or deleted countries, can produce wrong days-since values. Need a definition of meaningful that excludes bulk or mass-logged entries and handles null dates, and a visible 'based on logged engagements only' label with the last-engagement date so users do not read it as a relationship verdict.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: Proposer labels the rule deterministic and explainable but does not address data quality: bulk entries, missing dates, or staff who do not log. A1 and A4 'logged reasonably consistently' is untested.

challenges.challenge_text: Turnover: the digest goes to the 'existing Country-to-Coordinator relationship'. With frequent staff turnover, countries with no assigned coordinator, or whose coordinator has departed or is inactive, will drop out of every digest, so the countries most at risk, the ones nobody owns, are never alerted. Likewise 'last contact/owner' may show a departed person or a ministry contact who has since left, which sends staff to the wrong person. Need a fallback recipient (Operations lead) for unowned or inactive-owner countries, and the list should flag unassigned countries and stale contact records.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: Not addressed; the proposal assumes the assignments are current and complete.

challenges.challenge_text: A single 90-day threshold across ~100 countries ignores the fact that engagement cadence differs by relationship tier and region. High-priority partners may be effectively cold after 30 days, while low-touch countries are normal at 180 days. Result: priority countries decay unnoticed for a quarter while low-priority ones flood the list, which feeds the fatigue in C2. Also there is no check of the threshold against actual data before launch. Need a pre-launch backfill run on historical engagements to show the projected list size, and an agreed cap or an exit criterion if the list exceeds a limit, rather than learning from noise in production.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: Proposer defers tuning to after launch with engineering change only; no pre-launch validation against historical data.

assumptions.rationale: A deterministic rule on existing Engagement data needs no new entry or model. Excluding bulk and weak types blocks the clock-reset problem at zero UI cost.

assumptions.statement: A single 90-day threshold is acceptable for v1, validated by a pre-launch backfill dry run before release.
assumptions.rationale: Tiered thresholds would need a tier field, a UI and maintenance by busy coordinators. The backfill gives evidence on volume without adding schema.

assumptions.statement: The audience is Operations and Regional Coordinators, who need a weekly push of newly cold countries plus an always-available pull list. Countries without an active coordinator route to the existing Operations role.
assumptions.rationale: Weekly cadence fits the pace of decay. A deterministic fallback to an existing role covers unowned countries with no new screens or tables.

assumptions.statement: The existing Country-to-Coordinator assignment and Country/Mission access model can be reused for the list query and for the digest recipient check at send time. Email content is kept minimal because email leaves the CRM's access controls.
assumptions.rationale: Reuse avoids custom RBAC. Minimal digest content limits exposure outside the CRM.

assumptions.statement: Some countries are legitimately quiet. The digest lists a country once per cold episode, so low-touch countries appear at most once per episode and then live only on the pull list.
assumptions.rationale: Stateless newly-cold detection bounds fatigue without dormant flags. A new engagement resets the date, so re-crossings are re-alerted naturally.

success_criteria: Nightly job completes for all ~100 Countries in under 10 minutes. The Cold Countries list matches an independent SQL check of the rule (including bulk, null-date and future-date exclusions) for 100% of 20 sampled countries in UAT.
Zero new required fields or manual steps for Regional Coordinators in any existing form.

Backfill gate before release: the projected cold list is at most 30% of countries, and projected newly-cold countries are at most 5 per coordinator per week on average. If either is exceeded, the constant is adjusted before launch.

Authorization test: a user scoped to country subset S sees zero Cold Countries rows or contact names outside S. The digest contains zero contact names. A user whose assignment is removed before send time receives no digest in 100% of test cases.
Every Country with no active coordinator and newly cold appears in the Operations digest in 100% of test cases, and is labelled 'Unassigned' in the list.
Pilot of 4 weeks: at least 50% of countries flagged newly cold receive a new meaningful Engagement within 30 days of first alert.
Ships as derived fields, one list view and one email job, with no new tables.

challenge_responses.response: The Critic is right that email is outside the access model. The fix needs no new screens, tables or manual steps. The list query filters by the viewer's existing Country scope, and derived fields are read through the same permission layer. Contact names appear in-app only if the viewer already has Contact access. The digest carries country name and days-since only, and recipients are re-checked at send time. Whether country names in email are permitted at all is a data-classification question for a human owner, not a product decision. If email is disallowed, the digest becomes a notification linking to the in-app list.

Newly cold needs no alert-state table or extra field. The nightly job already knows last meaningful engagement date. A country is newly cold in the weekly digest iff that date falls 90 to 97 days before the send. It is listed once per cold episode, and any new engagement resets the date, so re-crossings are alerted again naturally. This bounds fatigue because a low-touch country appears in the push digest once per episode, not every week, and thereafter only on the pull list. I decline the admin low-touch boolean for v1. It is a manual maintenance step that will rot, needs an edit surface and an owner, and the Critic's own concern about permanent re-listing disappears once the digest is episode-based. I also replace the loose '15 per coordinator' criterion with the backfill gate of at most 5 newly cold per coordinator per week. If the pilot shows persistent noise, a dormant flag can be added in v1.1 with real data.

Most of this is cheap and deterministic. I drop staff-logged email from meaningful types, leaving meeting, call and mission visit. I exclude engagements linked to more than 5 Countries as bulk entries, ignore null and future dates, and skip merged or deleted Countries. The list now carries a static 'Based on logged engagements only' label and the last-engagement date, so the rule is not read as a relationship verdict. None of this adds a screen, table or coordinator step. What I do not fix is under-logging by staff who never record calls. That is a data-habit issue the product cannot solve in v1, and the label and the backfill make it visible.

Unowned countries are the highest-risk case, so I add a deterministic fallback. Countries with no active coordinator (none assigned, or the assignee is inactive per existing user status) go in the digest to users holding the existing Operations role, and the list shows an 'Unassigned' label. No new role, screen or table is needed. For stale contacts, the list shows the last contact only if the contact is active in existing status data. Building a role-change or staleness tracker is out, since that is the historical role graph I am cutting.

I reject per-tier or per-region thresholds in v1. They need a tier attribute on Country, someone to maintain it, and a config UI, and the tier assignment is itself an institutional priority decision for humans, not the product. A single constant is changeable by engineering in one line. I do accept the substance of the pre-launch check, since it costs no schema or UI: a one-time backfill dry run on historical engagements is now a release gate with a numeric limit (cold list at most 30% of countries, at most 5 newly cold per coordinator per week). If the gate fails, the constant is changed before launch instead of learning from noise in production. Together with the stateless once-per-episode digest, this answers the fatigue concern without tiering.

challenges.challenge_text: Residual risk: country names and 'gone cold' status in an email leave the CRM's access controls, and a coordinator's mailbox may be forwarded or retained.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: The engineering fixes are adequate for an MVP. The list is filtered by the viewer's Country scope, contact names show only with existing Contact access, the digest carries country name and days-since only, and recipients are re-checked at send time. Whether country names may appear in email at all is a data-classification decision that engineering cannot settle. The Proposer already has a fallback: a link-only notification if email is disallowed.

challenges.challenge_text: The stateless 90-to-97-day window silently drops countries. (1) If the weekly send fails, is delayed, or runs on a different weekday than the nightly job, a country that crossed 90 days in that week is never digested. Its last engagement date moves past the 97-day window, and the only trace is the pull list. (2) A country that crosses day 90 while suppressed (active Mission or future-dated Engagement) is outside the window by the time suppression lifts. The digest never announces it, and it may be the one nobody is watching. (3) Inclusive 90 and 97 on an integer day count gives an 8-day span, so a country can appear in two consecutive digests.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: The episode-based approach does answer the weekly re-listing of low-touch countries, and declining the admin boolean for v1 is acceptable. But the claim that it is bounded and reliable holds only if every run succeeds and no suppression overlaps the window. The 'at most once per episode' guarantee is not actually enforced. A cheap fix needs no new table: either add a derived 'last digested cold-episode date' field on Country, or define the window half-open [90,97) tied to the actual run date, with a run-failure alert and a catch-up rule. Also define how a country whose suppression lifts after the window is surfaced.

challenges.challenge_text: Cold status could be read as a relationship verdict, and the clock can be reset by weak or bulk engagements, or distorted by null/future dates and merged or deleted Countries.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: This is adequate for an MVP. Email is removed from the meaningful types. Entries linked to more than 5 Countries are excluded. Null and future dates are ignored, and merged or deleted Countries are skipped. The list carries the 'Based on logged engagements only' label and the last-engagement date. Under-logging by staff is a data-habit problem that the label and backfill make visible and that the product cannot solve. Excluding legitimate multi-country meetings may over-alert slightly, which is acceptable in the safe direction.

challenges.challenge_text: Countries with no coordinator or an inactive one drop out of every digest, and the list could show a departed contact or owner.

The last contact appears only if it is active in existing status data. A role-change tracker is correctly out of scope for the MVP.

assumptions.statement: The existing Country-to-Coordinator assignment and Country/Mission access model can be reused for the list query and the digest recipient check at send time. Email content is kept minimal because email leaves the CRM's access controls. Whether country names may appear in email at all is escalated to a human data-classification owner. If disallowed, the digest becomes a link-only notification.
assumptions.rationale: Reuse avoids custom RBAC. Minimal digest content limits exposure outside the CRM. The classification decision is not ours to make.

assumptions.statement: Some countries are legitimately quiet. The digest lists a country once per cold episode, tracked by one derived date field on Country (the last engagement date for which a digest was sent). Low-touch countries therefore appear in the push digest once per episode and then live only on the pull list.
assumptions.rationale: One derived field makes once-per-episode alerting idempotent and robust to missed runs and suppression overlap. It needs no new table, UI or coordinator step, and no dormant flag.

success_criteria: Nightly job completes for all ~100 Countries in under 10 minutes. The Cold Countries list matches an independent SQL check of the rule (including bulk, null-date and future-date exclusions) for 100% of 20 sampled countries in UAT.
Zero new required fields or manual steps for Regional Coordinators in any existing form.

Backfill gate before release: the projected cold list is at most 30% of countries, and projected newly-cold countries are at most 5 per coordinator per week on average. If either is exceeded, the constant is adjusted before launch.

Digest reliability tests: (a) after a simulated skipped or failed weekly send, 100% of countries that went cold in that period appear in the next successful digest. (b) A country whose suppression lifts while still cold appears in the next digest. (c) No country appears in two digests within the same cold episode, across 100% of test cases. (d) A new meaningful engagement followed by a re-crossing triggers a fresh alert.

Authorization test: a user scoped to country subset S sees zero Cold Countries rows or contact names outside S. The digest contains zero contact names. A user whose assignment is removed before send time receives no digest in 100% of test cases.
Every Country with no active coordinator and newly cold appears in the Operations digest in 100% of test cases, and is labelled 'Unassigned' in the list.
Pilot of 4 weeks: at least 50% of countries flagged newly cold receive a new meaningful Engagement within 30 days of first alert.
Ships as derived fields on Country, one list view and one email job, with no new tables.

challenge_responses.response: The Critic's R2 argument is new and exposes a real flaw in my 90-to-97-day window: a failed or delayed send, a suppression that overlaps the window, or the inclusive-boundary span can each drop a country silently or list it twice. The fix adds zero tables, screens or coordinator steps: one derived field on Country, digest_stamped_for_date, written by the job. A country is digested iff it is cold, unsuppressed at send time, and the stamp differs from its current last meaningful engagement date. The stamp is written only after a successful send handoff. This is idempotent: failed or late sends retry on the next run, and countries released from suppression surface in the first digest after the lift. The stamp cannot cause double listing, and a new engagement changes the date so a re-crossing re-alerts. The backfill script stamps already-cold countries at launch to avoid a first-week flood. I still decline the admin low-touch boolean and snooze. They are manual maintenance steps that will rot, and episode-based alerting already removes the weekly re-listing the Critic raised. A dormant flag can be reconsidered in v1.1 if pilot data shows persistent noise.

challenges.challenge_text: Whether country names may appear in email at all is a data-classification decision for the institution, not an engineering call. The Proposer has already made the engineering mitigations: list filtered by viewer scope, no contact names in the digest, and recipients re-checked at send time.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: Engineering mitigations are adequate for an MVP. The residual question (country names in email, with a link-only fallback) is correctly escalated to the data-classification owner. Status stays escalated and is not reopened.

challenges.challenge_text: The stamp design (digest_stamped_for_date compared with the last meaningful engagement date) fixes weekly re-listing for countries that have engagements. It breaks for a Country with no qualifying engagement at all, such as a small partner with only email logs, or one whose only engagements are bulk entries. Its last meaningful engagement date is null and the stamp is also null. The inclusion rule says 'differs ... or is null', so the country is included every week. After a send the stamp is set to a null date, which changes nothing. These never-engaged countries, likely a sizeable share of ~100, would reappear in every digest forever. That is the alert fatigue C2 was raised about. The launch backfill cannot stamp them either, because a null stamp is indistinguishable from unstamped.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: The revision is a real improvement. It makes alerting idempotent, handles failed sends and suppression lifts, and gives re-alerting on re-crossing. Declining the admin low-touch boolean is acceptable, since once-per-episode alerting removes most of the weekly noise. One solvable gap remains: the null-date case. The fix needs no new table or UI. Use a fixed sentinel stamp value (for example a constant 'never engaged' date) so that null-date countries are digested once and then stamped. Or exclude never-engaged countries from the push digest and keep them on the pull list. Please state which, and add a test case for it.

challenges.challenge_text: Already resolved: the 'meaningful' definition excludes staff-logged email, bulk entries linked to more than 5 Countries, and null or future dates. Merged or deleted countries are skipped, and the list carries the 'Based on logged engagements only' label.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: The Proposer's revision removes the clock-reset and bad-date risks. Status stays accepted.

challenges.challenge_text: Already resolved: countries with no active coordinator route to the existing Operations role and are labelled 'Unassigned'. Contact display is gated by the viewer's Contact access and active status.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: The fallback recipient and the unassigned flag cover the turnover risk for an MVP. Status stays accepted.

challenges.challenge_text: Already resolved: a pre-launch backfill dry run is now a release gate, with caps of at most 30% of countries cold and at most 5 newly cold per coordinator per week. Exceeding either cap triggers adjusting the constant.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: The backfill gate and exit criterion answer the original challenge. Status stays accepted.

C1.challenge_text: The weekly digest and 'Cold Countries' list inherit the 'existing Country access model', but the list shows 'last contact/owner' and the digest is sent by email. A Regional Coordinator for Region X, or a staff member scoped to only a few countries, could see contact names for countries outside their assignment if the list view or batch-written derived fields on Country bypass per-record permission checks. The digest also puts country names and contact identities into email, which leaves the CRM's access controls and may be forwarded or retained in personal mailboxes. If a coordinator's access is revoked after reassignment, the digest could still arrive. Needs explicit enforcement: list query filtered by the viewer's country scope, digest content minimal (country name and days only, no contact names), and recipients re-evaluated at send time.

C2.challenge_text: Alert fatigue: 'occasional false positive is tolerable' is unsupported, and there is no snooze or dormant flag. Many of ~100 countries are legitimately low-touch (no active projects, small partners), so the same countries will reappear on the list every week and coordinators will learn to ignore the digest. The 'newly cold' wording is also ambiguous, since without alert state (no new tables) the job cannot reliably tell newly cold from still cold, so it will either re-list the same countries weekly or miss re-crossings. Suppression covers only active missions or future engagements. The success criterion of up to 15 countries per coordinator on average is itself a noisy digest. Need a bounded way to identify 'newly cold' (for example a derived field on Country holding the date it first went cold) and a cheap way to exclude known low-touch countries (for example a single boolean on Country set by an admin).

C3.challenge_text: Equating 'cold' with no logged engagement conflates the relationship with the logging habits of staff. Countries whose engagements are held by a coordinator who left, or handled by a delegate who never logs calls, will show cold when the relationship is warm, and a warm-looking country will appear healthy because of one trivial staff-logged email. Also, 'email logged by staff' and any engagement type counting as meaningful lets a bulk or automated mass mailing to 100 countries reset the clock for everyone, hiding genuinely cold countries. Also, engagement records with a null or future date, or merged or deleted countries, can produce wrong days-since values. Need a definition of meaningful that excludes bulk or mass-logged entries and handles null dates, and a visible 'based on logged engagements only' label with the last-engagement date so users do not read it as a relationship verdict.

C4.challenge_text: Turnover: the digest goes to the 'existing Country-to-Coordinator relationship'. With frequent staff turnover, countries with no assigned coordinator, or whose coordinator has departed or is inactive, will drop out of every digest, so the countries most at risk, the ones nobody owns, are never alerted. Likewise 'last contact/owner' may show a departed person or a ministry contact who has since left, which sends staff to the wrong person. Need a fallback recipient (Operations lead) for unowned or inactive-owner countries, and the list should flag unassigned countries and stale contact records.

C5.challenge_text: A single 90-day threshold across ~100 countries ignores the fact that engagement cadence differs by relationship tier and region. High-priority partners may be effectively cold after 30 days, while low-touch countries are normal at 180 days. Result: priority countries decay unnoticed for a quarter while low-priority ones flood the list, which feeds the fatigue in C2. Also there is no check of the threshold against actual data before launch. Need a pre-launch backfill run on historical engagements to show the projected list size, and an agreed cap or an exit criterion if the list exceeds a limit, rather than learning from noise in production.

final_decision.feature_request: The CRM should alert us when our relationship with a country goes cold.
final_decision.executive_summary: v1 derives a 'last meaningful engagement' date for each country from existing Engagement records and flags a country as cold after 90 days without one. Flagged countries appear on an in-app Cold Countries list that is filtered by the viewer's country scope and labelled 'Based on logged engagements only'. Countries with no active coordinator are marked 'Unassigned'. The main trade-off argued was alert noise and reliability against keeping v1 free of new tables, settings screens and manual dormant flags. The Proposer chose one derived stamp field and one global threshold with a backfill release gate. The Critic accepted the definition of 'meaningful', the unowned-country handling and the threshold gate. Two items need a human decision before the weekly email digest can be scoped: whether country names may appear in email at all (C1), and how never-engaged countries are handled in the digest (C2, where the agents deadlocked).
agreed_scope_included: Derive 'last meaningful engagement date' per Country from existing Engagement records, with no new data entry. Meaningful means type meeting, call or mission visit. Staff-logged email is excluded. Engagements with a null or future date are ignored. Engagements linked to more than 5 Countries are excluded as bulk entries (config constant). Merged or deleted Countries are skipped.
Fixed system-wide 'cold' rule: no meaningful engagement with a Country in the last 90 days (a single config constant, no UI screen).
Nightly batch job writing cold status, last meaningful engagement date and days-since as derived fields on Country. All reads go through the existing record-permission query layer.

In-app 'Cold Countries' list view, sortable by days since last engagement. It shows Country, last engagement date, last contact (only if the viewer has existing Contact access and the contact is active in existing status data) and coordinator. Countries with no active coordinator show an 'Unassigned' label. The list is filtered by the viewer's existing Country scope and carries the static label 'Based on logged engagements only'.

One-time pre-launch backfill dry run on historical engagements, run as a script with no UI. It reports the projected cold list size as a release gate, and the constant is adjusted before launch if the gate is exceeded.
Alert visibility reuses the existing Country/Mission access model; no new permissions or roles. Job failures are reported through existing job-failure monitoring.
agreed_scope_excluded: Per-country, per-tier or per-region thresholds and any settings UI (v1 uses one constant, tuned after the backfill and pilot data).
Admin-set 'low-touch' or 'dormant' boolean, snooze, acknowledge, or any coordinator-facing manual workflow.
New tables for alert state, relationship history, or historical role graphs. The one derived date field on Country is the only alert state.
ML or weighted relationship-health scoring, sentiment analysis, or predicted churn.
Automatic capture from email, calendar or phone systems.
Escalation chains, approval workflows, or task assignment from alerts.
Stale-contact detection beyond the existing contact status field, and role-change tracking for ministry contacts or project leads.
Real-time, push, SMS or chat notifications.
Building new job-monitoring infrastructure. The send job reuses existing failure alerting.
Judging diplomatic sensitivity of why a relationship is quiet, and deciding whether country names may appear in email. Both are human policy and data-classification decisions.

surfaced_assumptions.assumption: 'Cold' means no recent meaningful logged engagement, not a verdict on relationship quality. Meaningful excludes staff-logged email, bulk or mass entries (linked to more than 5 Countries), and null or future dates.
surfaced_assumptions.resolution_notes: C3 challenged clock-reset and bad-date risks. The Proposer revised the definition of meaningful and added the 'Based on logged engagements only' label, and the Critic accepted.

surfaced_assumptions.assumption: A single 90-day threshold is acceptable for v1, validated by a pre-launch backfill dry run before release.
surfaced_assumptions.resolution_notes: C5 asked for tiered thresholds and pre-launch validation. The Proposer defended the single threshold and added a numeric backfill release gate, and the Critic accepted.

surfaced_assumptions.resolution_notes: C4 raised unowned countries and departed owners. The Proposer added the Operations-role fallback and the 'Unassigned' label, and the Critic accepted.

surfaced_assumptions.resolution_notes: C1 engineering mitigations were accepted as adequate (scope-filtered list, no contact names in digest, send-time recipient check). The residual question of country names in email was escalated to humans in R2 and stayed escalated.

surfaced_assumptions.resolution_notes: C2 went through three rounds and the Proposer revised to the stamp-field design. A null-date gap remained open and the gate escalated it as a deadlock (DEADLOCK_ESCALATED).

open_questions_for_humans: [C1] Data-classification owner (with Legal / Information Security): may country names and 'gone cold' status appear in the weekly digest email at all? If yes, the digest carries country name and days-since only. If no, the digest becomes a link-only notification to the in-app list. The weekly digest (content, recipients and Operations fallback) is not in agreed scope until this is decided.

[C2] Product Manager together with the Operations lead: the agents could not agree on how the once-per-episode digest handles countries with no qualifying engagement (null last-engagement date). Proposer position: a derived digest_stamped_for_date field on Country makes alerts once per cold episode and robust to failed sends and suppression lifts, and no admin low-touch boolean or snooze is needed in v1 (the Proposer did not respond to the null-date case before the deadlock). Critic position: the design is an improvement, but never-engaged countries have a null stamp and would be listed in every weekly digest forever, so either a fixed sentinel stamp (digest once, then stamp) or exclusion of never-engaged countries from the push digest (pull list only) is needed, with a test case. Decision needed: which of those two approaches, if either, should apply, and is the stamp-field design acceptable as the basis for the digest? The digest, its suppression rule and the launch-time stamping are not in agreed scope until this is decided.
